criteria.label_table: Benchmark REFUTED iff KISS-GP wins >= 2 of 4 domains or dense KRR wins >= 1 of 4 domains in RMSE at equal-or-lower cost envelope; ties reported; no cherry-picked exclusions.
criteria.tie_reporting: the plan's label table states only 'ties reported'; the 0.5% relative tieband is an ANALYSIS operationalization of that rule, not a plan term. Sensitivity: grf-2d RE+SSAM +0.47% sits AT the 0.5% threshold (a tighter band flips it to a loss). The benchmark verdict is CONDITIONAL on the tieband application (per reviewer-B fix 6). Resolution (a) adopted: dense-vs-PCG on grf-2d is a TIE under the 0.5% band, because dense Cholesky and PCG solve the IDENTICAL masked-Gram system (P_m K P_m^T + lambda I) w = y_m on the same valid-cell domain - dense exactly (n_sub = n_observed = full observed cells) and PCG to KKT rel-res ~1e-6 - so the RMSE delta 4.85e-07 relative (dense 0.0809996662 vs pcg 0.0809997055) is a solver-tolerance artifact, not a method-level win. Dense is additionally at LOWER cost (median 0.154 s vs pcg 1.714 s). Sensitivity (disclosed): under a strict literal reading with NO tieband, dense_wins = 1 on grf-2d (numerically best AND cheaper) and the plan rule would make the benchmark REFUTED; this analysis reports not-refuted under resolution (a) with the identical-system justification on record. The 0.5% band now explicitly applies to BOTH RE+SSAM-vs-dense/PCG and dense-vs-PCG.
